source.description: One six-panel graphite-and-colored-pencil contact sheet intended to become five cumulative process frames and one finished master after full-sheet review.
source.notes: Keep one diagonal shooting star with its bright round head on the page right and exactly two tapered wake bands trailing toward the upper left above two layered pine-covered hill ridges. Include exactly five foreground pine silhouettes, exactly three small background stars, a broken foreground texture edge, tactile graphite, restrained indigo-blue and warm-yellow pencil, and no moon, buildings, people, text, labels, arrows, numbers, signature, watermark, border, or extra meteors.

process_strategy: Use six cumulative stages so the pale composition map, meteor and rough hill silhouettes, five-pine structure, sky and landscape detail, graphite-and-pencil value, and final reinforcement each have one distinct visible job. Reserve the meteor glow, two wake bands, five pine footprints, three star gaps, and foreground edge before dark hill or sky value so no finished keeper line or shading must be erased later.

final_elements.name: pale meteor ridge pine star and foreground composition map
final_elements.description: Light graphite places the meteor diagonal, round head, two wake routes, two hill ridges, exactly five pine footprints, three star centers, and a broken foreground edge.

final_elements.name: bright meteor head two tapered wake bands and two rough hill silhouettes
final_elements.description: A small bright meteor head and two tapering trails cross above two loose overlapping hill silhouettes while preserving every pale tree and star reserve.

final_elements.name: two refined hill ridges and exactly five foreground pine silhouettes
final_elements.description: Cleaner graphite settles both ridge contours and builds five varied pine silhouettes along the foreground ridge without covering the meteor or star gaps.

final_elements.name: three small sky stars pine branch rhythm distant hatching and broken foreground texture
final_elements.description: Exactly three small stars, simple branch strokes on all five pines, sparse distant-ridge hatching, and a broken rock-and-grass foreground edge complete the scene structure.

final_elements.name: graphite night values indigo-blue hills and warm-yellow meteor accents
final_elements.description: Directional graphite and restrained indigo-blue pencil deepen the established hills and sky pockets while warm yellow touches the established meteor head and wake; paper remains visible through every value.

overlap_reservations.background_lines_stop_before: The foreground ridge and its hatching stop at all five reserved pine trunks and branch masses; no finished hill texture is drawn beneath the pine silhouettes.

overlap_reservations.background_lines_stop_before: Sky graphite and indigo pencil stop around the reserved meteor head and both wake bands so their pale glow never requires erased finished shading.

overlap_reservations.background_lines_stop_before: Sky value stops around the three reserved star gaps, and foreground hatching stops at the broken rock-and-grass edge established in the map.

rejection_checks: Keep one diagonal meteor with its head on the page right and two wakes trailing toward the upper left, plus one crop and one scale in all six panels.
Keep one round meteor head, exactly two wake bands, two hill ridges, exactly five pines, exactly three small stars, and one broken foreground edge after those elements appear.
The meteor angle, hill contours, pine positions, star positions, and foreground edge may not drift between panels.
Sky and hill value must stop at the reserved meteor, wake, pine, and star footprints without requiring erased keeper lines.
Do not add a moon, cabin, tent, person, animal, extra meteor, extra pine, constellation line, readable text, label, arrow, number, signature, watermark, or decorative border.
The final panel may not introduce a meteor contour, wake band, hill, pine, star, foreground shape, hatch route, or color area.
The finish must retain believable graphite and colored-pencil tooth rather than vector-clean icon art, glossy AI poster art, digital airbrush gradients, or rasterized vector drawing.
